entries.10cfff3fddda84f0: A reportable segment that manufactures and sells automotive parts in the United States and Mexico. Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥77,591 million. Sales including inter-segment internal sales were ¥77,657 million (up 0.3% year on year), and operating profit was ¥4,402 million (down 38.5%). The securities report attributes the increase in sales to an increase in sales volume, and the decrease in operating profit to an increase in various expenses. In Mexico, because changes in the business environment meant the profit originally expected could no longer be anticipated, the carrying amounts of fixed assets such as automotive parts manufacturing equipment were reduced to their recoverable amounts, and an impairment loss of ¥1,805 million was recorded as an extraordinary loss. Franklin Precision Industry, Inc., a consolidated subsidiary in this segment, accounted for more than 10% of consolidated sales, with sales of ¥34,211 million (excluding inter-segment sales).

entries.38db3f91223e9a6d: Sales to Toyota Motor Corporation were 48.9% of revenue (¥161,847 million), and sales to Hyundai Motor Company were 10.4% (¥34,518 million). Revenue from the Toyota Group (including affiliates) was ¥185,117 million. The Group receives production plans from each delivery destination, starting with Toyota Motor Corporation, generally on a quarterly basis, and sets its own production plans taking its production capacity into account. The annual securities report states, in its business risks, that sales trends at Toyota Motor Corporation could affect the Group's results.
entries.3f38595c0430bb8b: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥330,834 million (down 1.9% year on year). Revenue from external customers was ¥135,780 million in Asia, ¥101,210 million in Japan, ¥77,591 million in the Americas and ¥16,251 million in Europe. The annual securities report states that revenue in Asia decreased due to lower sales volumes and the effect of exchange rates, while revenue in Japan and the Americas increased due to higher sales volumes. To make regional revenue easier to see, the figures show revenue from external customers rather than values that include internal revenue between segments.

entries.52f51a2f72def1d4: A reportable segment based in the Czech Republic, France and Belgium. Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥16,251 million. Sales including inter-segment internal sales were ¥16,288 million (up 1.9% year on year), and operating profit was ¥1,180 million (down 8.4%). The securities report attributes the increase in sales to the effect of exchange rates, and the decrease in operating profit to an increase in various expenses. Manufacturing and sales are carried out by Aisan Industry Czech s.r.o. in the Czech Republic, and Aisan Corporation Europe S.A. in Belgium is the base for sales activities in Europe. Aisan Industry France S.A.S., formerly a consolidated subsidiary, had all its shares transferred as of September 30, 2025, and was removed from the scope of consolidation.
entries.5736aaea54440427: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥18,287 million (down 0.3% year on year), ordinary profit was ¥19,229 million (down 0.3%), and net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥13,074 million (down 1.2%). Operating profit by region was ¥3,160 million in Japan (up 36.3%), ¥9,366 million in Asia (up 20.0%), ¥4,402 million in the Americas (down 38.5%) and ¥1,180 million in Europe (down 8.4%). In the Americas, because changes in the business environment meant that the revenue originally expected from automotive parts manufacturing facilities in Mexico could no longer be anticipated, an impairment loss of ¥1,805 million was recorded as an extraordinary loss. Net cash provided by operating activities was ¥7,204 million, a decrease of ¥21,018 million from the previous year.
entries.5eee77698e995ca3: It consists of the company and 25 consolidated subsidiaries, and conducts business in four regional reportable segments: Japan, Asia, the Americas and Europe. As changes in the scope of consolidation for the fiscal year ended March 2026, Aisan Autoparts India Co., Ltd. was merged into Aisan Industry India Co., Ltd. through absorption, and Aisan Industry France Co., Ltd. was excluded from consolidation following the transfer of all its shares. In April 2026, it acquired all shares of Toraisu Co., Ltd., and added that company and its subsidiaries to the Group.
entries.63b9b2c4820c2e17: A reportable segment that manufactures and sells automotive parts in South Korea, China, Indonesia, Thailand and India, and the one with the largest sales to external customers among the 4 reportable segments. Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥135,780 million. Sales including inter-segment internal sales were ¥136,979 million (down 5.8% year on year), and operating profit was ¥9,366 million (up 20.0%). The securities report attributes the decrease in sales to a decrease in sales volume and the effect of exchange rates, and the increase in operating profit to improved profitability. In its description of business, the securities report lists as the main affiliated companies in this region Hyundam Industrial Co., Ltd. in South Korea, AISAN INDUSTRY (TIANJIN) AUTO PARTS CO., LTD. and AISAN INDUSTRY (FOSHAN) AUTO PARTS CO., LTD. in China, PT. Aisan Nasmoco Industri in Indonesia, and Aisan Industry India Pvt. Ltd. in India, among others. Note that in sales to external customers this segment is larger than Japan, while in sales including inter-segment internal sales Japan is larger.

entries.7e9e9864c206c6dd: A reportable segment in which the Company mainly manufactures and sells automotive parts in Japan. In addition to automotive parts, this segment also conducts automobile transport brokerage, civil engineering and construction, and the development and sale of computer systems and programs. Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥101,210 million. Sales including inter-segment internal sales were ¥139,595 million (up 4.5% year on year), and operating profit was ¥3,160 million (up 36.3%). The securities report attributes the increase in sales to an increase in sales volume, and the increase in operating profit to improved profitability. The main affiliated companies in Japan are Teikei Carburetor Co., Ltd., Nichialloy Co., Ltd., Aisan Kumamoto Co., Ltd. (automotive parts), Aikyo Sangyo Co., Ltd. (transportation, etc.) and Aisan Computer Service Co., Ltd. (system development and calculation services). In September 2022, the Company took over the fuel pump module business from DENSO Corporation; the securities report states that the change to the Company's brand has been completed and that, from fiscal 2024, production that had been outsourced is being switched in stages to the Company's own production.
entries.7ee3f99957d741d1: Toyota Motor Corporation and Hyundai Motor Company (counterparties for which the securities report's information on major customers lists Asia as the related segment)
entries.8fbc99f66e25c5fb: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that the Group (the company, 25 consolidated subsidiaries, 2 unconsolidated subsidiaries and 1 associate) conducts business mainly in the manufacture and sale of automotive parts. Main products include fuel pump modules, throttle bodies and canisters; in Japan, the company mainly manufactures and sells them, and overseas the local subsidiaries in each country do so, for automakers in Japan and overseas. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥330,834 million (down 1.9% year on year), and revenue from automotive parts of ¥321,092 million broke down as follows: fuel system products ¥180,410 million, intake and exhaust system products ¥72,905 million, emission control system products ¥52,126 million, valve train system products (engine valves) ¥10,508 million, and other automotive parts ¥5,141 million. Sales to Toyota Motor Corporation, its main customer, account for 48.9% of revenue.

entries.d3bb9e3246d4b608: The annual securities report states that fuel pump modules, throttle bodies, canisters and EGR valves, which are important functional parts in the engine area, are designated as four priority products, with the aim of becoming the No.1 product in the world in each. In addition, it has started production of electrification products such as bus bar ends for batteries in hybrid vehicles, and is advancing research and development of clean energy utilization technologies such as ammonia and hydrogen power generation systems.
